name: cpg-limit-cycle
title: The CPG's Limit Cycle
question:
Is the walking rhythm a dynamical attractor of the CTRNN — does the network's
state trace a stable closed loop (a limit cycle), the signature of a central
pattern generator?
claim:
The evolved CTRNN's state traces a clean closed loop in its activity space — a
limit cycle — repeating once per stride (~19.8 steps). The rhythm is a
self-sustaining attractor, not a clocked or scripted sequence.

expected_behavior.name: ctrnn-state-traces-limit-cycle
expected_behavior.observable: closed-loop trajectory in CTRNN output space
expected_behavior.condition: committed walker seed, 500 steps, dt 0.1, record outputs
expected_behavior.rationale:
Projected onto two neurons, the recorded CTRNN output trajectory settles
onto a closed loop that repeats at the stride period — a limit cycle. The
neuron-output raster shows the same regular periodicity.

findings.summary: The CTRNN state settles onto a closed limit cycle repeating once per stride — the CPG attractor.
